paragraphs: Swamiji noticed that fanaticism comes in many shapes. Some people are fanatical about wine, others about cigars. Some are convinced that if only men stopped smoking cigars, the world would become paradise.

One day in his class in Chicago there was a young woman who belonged to a group of ladies running a settlement house. There they welcomed working people and offered them music and exercise classes. Good work, certainly.
While talking about the troubles of the world, she announced that she knew the remedy. Swamiji asked how she could be so sure. Her reply: had he seen Hull House?

For her, that one institution was the answer to every ill humanity suffers from. Swamiji felt sorry for her, because such a belief only tightens its grip over time. India has its own version, he added: people who believe that letting widows remarry would by itself cure every evil. Taking one good idea and treating it as the cure for everything, he said, is exactly what fanaticism is.
learn: It's great to be passionate about a cause, but no single fix solves every problem. Keep doing your good work while staying humble about how much it can do.
